analysis.time: Singapore Home Australia Sydney Melbourne Brisbane Perth Gold Coast Sunshine Coast Byron Bay Hobart Adelaide Townsville New Zealand New Zealand Auckland Christchurch Dunedin Queenstown Wellington Asia Bali Hong Kong Osaka Singapore Tokyo Rest of the world Barcelona Fiji London New York Paris Rome Explore U:L Home Locations Australia Sydney Melbourne Brisbane Perth Gold Coast Sunshine Coast Byron Bay Hobart Adelaide Townsville New Zealand New Zealand Auckland Christchurch Dunedin Queenstown Wellington Asia Bali Hong Kong Osaka Singapore Tokyo Rest of the world Barcelona Fiji London New York Paris Rome Best Of Singapore Things To Do Food & Drink Health + Wellness Local Escapes Search U:L Search U:L Best Of Singapore Things To Do Food & Drink Health + Wellness Local Escapes News Singapore Haze Update: Air Pollution Hits Very High Levels As N95 Masks Are Distributed 14th Oct 2026 Written by: Gracie Stewart Singapore and Bali Editor | Urban List Singapore’s haze situation has taken a concerning turn today (14 October, 20206), with air pollution levels reaching the Very High band for the first time this haze season.
analysis.location_and_population: The one-hour PM2.5 reading in the west surged to 284 micrograms per cubic metre at 2pm, while the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) remained in the unhealthy range across the island.
analysis.event: Air pollution levels reached Very High band, prompting the Government to distribute N95 masks to vulnerable groups.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) remained in the unhealthy range, with a one-hour PM2.5 reading of 284 micrograms per cubic metre. The 24-hour PSI could climb into the Very Unhealthy range. Eligible groups include seniors, CHAS cardholders, pregnant women, children aged seven to 16, and people with medical conditions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Government has brought forward the distribution of N95 masks and advised healthy individuals to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exercise when the 24-hour PSI is unhealthy.

analysis.brief_en: Singapore experienced a significant increase in air pollution, with the one-hour PM2.5 reading reaching 284 micrograms per cubic metre. The National Environment Agency (NEA) warned that the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) could rise to the Very Unhealthy range. In response, the Government distributed N95 masks to vulnerable groups, including seniors, CHAS cardholders, pregnant women, children aged seven to 16, and those with medical conditions. The NEA advised healthy individuals to reduce outdoor exercise when the PSI is unhealthy.

The National Environment Agency (NEA) warned that the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) could rise to the Very Unhealthy range. In response, the Government distributed N95 masks to vulnerable groups, including seniors, CHAS cardholders, pregnant women, children aged seven to 16, and those with medical conditions. The NEA advised healthy individuals to reduce outdoor exercise when the PSI is unhealthy.
